topics.topic: Credential value character grammar, control characters, whitespace, and wire encoding
questions: What exact character repertoire and byte encoding make a credential value valid for transmission as an HTTP header, and are leading or trailing whitespace allowed?
Which Unicode characters are valid in a credential value, what exactly counts as a control character, and how is an accepted non-ASCII value serialized on the wire?
Exactly which Unicode characters or encoded bytes count as control characters after UTF-8 decoding and removal of one trailing newline?

judgement.why: P1 judged the same credential character-repertoire, control-character, whitespace and wire-encoding question on the same passages.

precedent.topic: Credential newline stripping, forbidden characters, Unicode acceptance, and wire encoding
precedent.why: The exact newline sequence, character repertoire, and HTTP wire encoding are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Disclosure class assigned to empty mapped-operation output lists
questions: When a mapped operation receives an empty list, does each empty output list take the binding output port's declared class or the highest class among the node's inputs?
What disclosure class does an empty output list from a mapped operation node receive?
When a mapped operation receives an empty list, is each empty output list classified from the binding output declaration or from the node's inputs?

quotes:
A binding output is not carried from the operation's inputs: it takes the
   class the binding declares, which the owner accepted with the binding (A08),
   whatever its inputs' classes — at proof time, at run time, and for the empty
   lists of a mapped operation over an empty list alike.

each list of the highest class among its elements (A07); an empty list
   takes the highest class among the node's inputs — the list it mapped over
   and every other input — as an execution of the node would have received
   them (M21), so no class is lowered;
judgement.why: One passage assigns the binding output's declared class to an empty mapped-operation output, while the other assigns the highest class among the node's inputs.

topics.topic: Eligibility and retry rules for unmapped nodes with concluded executions or waiting points
questions: For an unmapped node whose inputs still hold values, what state excludes it from selection after it has concluded or while it waits, and under which explicit resume, approval or resolution event may it become executable again?
Is an unmapped node with a concluded NodeExecution or an active WaitingPoint excluded from `ready_nodes`, and exactly when does an approval, resolution or resume make a waiting node eligible again?
What precisely makes an element eligible for another attempt despite an existing immutable NodeExecution, and what does “concluded record” mean here?

judgement.why: P7 judged the same scheduler eligibility and retry question for concluded and waiting elements on the same texts.

precedent.topic: Scheduler eligibility, semantic finality, and retry rules for concluded or waiting nodes and mapped elements
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] MUST read the Run by identity, its pinned graph with read_flow_version, and its trace with read_records through ExecutionsOfRun, and derive every element's conclusion from the trace: a function element from its NodeExecution's status, an operation element from operation_element_conclusion. If any NodeExecution of the run is refused_by_owner it reaches nothing and ends the run refused. Otherwise it executes one node at a time until no node can execute, then writes the rest or end state in one RecordRunProgressChange.

advance_run: [BEHAVIOR] A function element is executed with execute_function_element; an operation element is reached with reach_operation_element, given a RunContext of the run_id, the pinned flow_version_id and started_under the store_position of the FlowActivation read with ActivationBeforeRun, whose absence is raised as StoreInternalError; operation elements that wait are not reached again here.

operation_element_conclusion: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] Decides from the latest NodeExecution of the element, the one with the highest attempt_number, in this order: succeeded concludes succeeded with that record's outputs; outcome_unknown with its EffectAttempt applied concludes succeeded with no outputs when the binding has no output ports and otherwise failed with status outcome_unknown and detail applied_outputs_unknown; any status other than succeeded, service_unreachable and outcome_unknown concludes failed with that status and detail_code; then an approval of the element with status requested makes it wait with reason owner_approval and that approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt resolved not_applied waits with reason owner_approval and no approval_id; then outcome_unknown with its attempt unknown waits with reason outcome_unknown; then service_unreachable waits with reason service_unreachable; with no NodeExecution and no requested approval the element is not reached.

advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text. A mapped node, once selected, takes its elements in list order, executing every element with no concluded record that does not wait, before the next node is selected; a waiting or failed element does not stop the elements after it, and a concluded element is never executed again.
precedent.why: The later run contract derives semantic conclusions from the trace, excludes waiting operation elements from ordinary advancement, forbids re-executing concluded elements, and classifies resolved `not_applied` as waiting for approval.

topics.topic: Exact handling of trailing newlines in credential files
questions: Exactly which terminal byte or character sequence is removed from a credential file, and what happens when more than one such sequence is present?
Does one trailing newline mean one LF byte only, one CRLF sequence, either Unicode line ending, or all trailing newline sequences?

judgement.why: P11 judged the same question about the exact trailing-newline removal rule for credential files.

precedent.topic: Credential newline removal and control-character normalization rules
precedent.why: The exact newline byte sequence and control-character repertoire are encoding and field-constraint decisions for State 6.

topics.topic: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to executable nodes
questions: After a node concludes and causes skips or `upstream_failed` conclusions, are all newly forced records written before selecting the next ready executable node, after that node executes, or only when no executable nodes remain?
When execution makes some nodes non-executable while other nodes are ready, in what deterministic order are derived records and executable nodes processed?

judgement.why: P3 judged the same ordering question for derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to ready-node execution.

precedent.topic: Ordering of derived skip and upstream-failure records relative to ready-node execution
quotes: advance_run: [ORCHESTRATION] After each function element MUST write one RecordRunProgressChange holding that element's execution, its StoredValues and SpooledFiles, and every skipped_by_guard and upstream_failed record that became determined, executions sorted by (node_id, map_index), with status running; after an operation element, whose concluding record effects wrote, the next RecordRunProgressChange holds the records it made non-executable.
precedent.why: The later run contract requires newly determined skipped and upstream-failed records to be written immediately after the element that determined them, before the advancement loop selects another executable node.

topics.topic: Revalidation of configuration-file protections during token-list reload
questions: When the configuration changes during operation, must the kernel revalidate A17's file ownership, mode and file-type requirements before accepting the new token list?

When the token list is re-read after startup, must the kernel recheck the configuration file's regular-file, no-symlink, ownership and permission conditions, and what happens if only those attributes change while its bytes do not?

quotes:
Before evaluating each request the kernel reads the configuration file and
   compares the SHA-256 of its bytes with that of the last read; when they differ,
   or the file cannot be read, it re-reads it (K-15) and takes from it only the
   token list.

Exactly four checks apply to a re-read: the
   file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two
   tokens are equal; no two agent tokens share a name (M28).

Every other field of the configuration, and every other start check, applies
   only at a restart.
judgement.why: The live re-read applies exactly the four listed token checks, while the file-protection start checks apply only at restart.

topics.topic: Unit and truncation stage used for redacted failure-detail length
questions: Is the disclosed length measured in Unicode characters, UTF-8 bytes before truncation, or stored UTF-8 bytes after truncation?
Is the reported failure-detail length measured in UTF-8 bytes, Unicode code points, or another unit, and is it measured before or after A20 truncation?

judgement.why: P4 judged the same failure-detail length unit and truncation-stage question.

precedent.topic: Unit and truncation basis for disclosed failure-detail length
quotes: handle_get_repair_view: [FIELD_ASSIGNMENT] The class of a NodeExecution is the highest class among the items of its inputs, each SpooledFilesRef counting with its disclosure_class even when empty, and when its executed names a binding also of its outputs; the class of an operation execution's failure_detail is the highest of that class and the disclosure classes read_binding declares for that binding's outputs; the class of a TrialExecution is the highest class among its TrialCase's inputs (A07 rule 5, A09 rule 7); a failure_detail becomes DetailLength with its UTF-8 byte length and that class when the reader is an agent and the class is above open, and DetailText otherwise, always for the owner.
precedent.why: The later note specifies the UTF-8 byte length of the retained failure_detail.

topics.topic: Whether a waiting element is schedulable before its release event
questions: Can a waiting element be selected and executed during ordinary advancement, or only when the specific approval, resolution or resume action releases or retries it?
Does “can still execute” mean it is schedulable while its WaitingPoint exists, or only that it may become schedulable after a later approval, resolution or resume?

judgement.why: P7 judged the same question about whether waiting elements are schedulable before the specific event that releases or retries them.

topics.topic: Whether secrecy guarantees cover encoded or transformed credential echoes
questions: Is the State 0 no-secret-in-an-answer guarantee limited to the credential's verbatim bytes, or must encoded or otherwise transformed credential values also be withheld?
May a service response containing an encoded form of a credential enter stored values, traces or answers, or must the State 0 no-secret guarantee also cover encoded forms?

quotes:
- **Secrets** — service credentials and tokens live in the installation's
  protected configuration; they never enter a function, a flow, a trace or an
  answer.

A service's own answer is not the
   kernel's text: a body that echoes the value verbatim, 2xx or not, is
   withheld and never used as an output (A09 rule 7); one that carries it in
   another encoding is not recognised, and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: State 0 says credentials never enter an answer, while A17 permits an encoded credential echo to be handled and disclosed according only to its class.

topics.topic: Disclosure class when trial or execution input and output sets are empty
questions: What class is assigned to an expected output or computed execution class when the relevant input and output sets are empty?

topics.topic: Node outcome when one upstream branch is disabled and another remains unresolved
questions: If one input is permanently disabled by a guard or skipped source and another input comes from a waiting source, is the node recorded skipped immediately, kept unresolved, or later changed to upstream_failed if that source fails?

topics.topic: Persistence location for the disclosure class of an empty many-file output
questions: Where is the disclosure class of an empty `many` file output recorded so it can be recovered after restart and used by A07?

topics.topic: Redaction representation for personal-data file lists
questions: For a `many` personal-data file value, does the agent receive one redacted entry per file, preserving count and order, or one redaction for the list as a whole; if the latter, what digest identifies the list?

topics.topic: Storage and disclosure of bounded trial-execution failure details
questions: Do trial executions retain a bounded failure detail; if so, in which model field is it stored and subjected to A07 disclosure?

topics.topic: Whether agents may submit full personal-data values
questions: May an agent submit the full content of a value whose declared or assigned class is personal_data, or must such requests be refused or restricted to the owner?

topics.topic: Whether credential secrecy is provenance-based or applies to identical ordinary data
questions: Is the secrecy guarantee provenance-based, excluding only the value read as a credential, or must the kernel detect and withhold every byte-for-byte occurrence of that value regardless of its source?

topics.topic: Whether manifest required-header values must be non-secret and how that is enforced
questions: Must manifest required-header values be guaranteed non-secret, and if so, how is that requirement established or enforced before they are exposed in previews and responses?
